caseStudies.application: Original BLA for adult recurrent respiratory papillomatosis
caseStudies.phase: Phase 1/2, single-arm, 32 treated patients at year one
caseStudies.evidence: Sponsor-reported 26/32 experienced fewer surgical interventions and 23/32 had reductions of 50% or more; durability with variable denominators. No randomized comparison.
caseStudies.benefitRisk: Reduced repeated airway surgeries would matter clinically; uncertainty from uncontrolled efficacy and variability in response.
caseStudies.regulatory: FDA accepted accelerated-review BLA but explicitly flagged eligibility; FDA had already approved PAPZIMEOS for RRP. Sponsor warned eligibility might fail without evidence of meaningful advantage over available therapy. Unknown inspection/CMC evidence treated as unknown, not failure.
caseStudies.rationale: A sponsor-disclosed, unresolved accelerated-approval pathway challenge is more immediately decisive than an uncontrolled surgery-benefit signal, even though approval remains possible.

caseStudies.application: Original NDA, adult chronic hepatitis B
caseStudies.phase: Two randomized, double-blind pivotal Phase 3 studies (B-Well 1 / B-Well 2), replication across trials.
caseStudies.evidence: Sustained functional cure at week 72 occurred in approximately 19-20% of active-treated versus no placebo patients. Replication and statistically positive trial endpoints support efficacy.
caseStudies.benefitRisk: Functional cure is consequential, although most treated patients did not reach cure. Liver enzyme elevations and higher severe adverse events require monitoring and careful labeling.
caseStudies.regulatory: Priority Review and breakthrough designation, with two pivotal efficacy trials. Unknown FDA inspections and manufacturing review are missing evidence, not assumed failures.
caseStudies.rationale: Two independent positive pivotal trials on a clinically meaningful endpoint outweigh the manageable but nontrivial safety signal, without evidence of a known disqualifying regulatory issue.

caseStudies.application: Supplemental NDA 217759/S-006, ages 4–11 weighing at least 27kg
caseStudies.phase: Single-arm, open-label pediatric Phase 3 study; earlier randomized clinical evidence and approval for ages 12+ already established.
caseStudies.evidence: Pediatric 12-week study reported improvements in naïve B cells and lymphadenopathy consistent with mechanistic activity. Trial lacks randomized pediatric control.
caseStudies.benefitRisk: Meaningful rare-disease unmet need and established benefit in older patients support exposure-bridged pediatric labeling; pediatric dataset is small.
caseStudies.regulatory: Earlier Jan 2026 CRL concerned underexposure in lighter children and an analytical production-test method. Subsequent resubmission specifically excluded under-27kg patients and included additional analytical-method data after FDA meeting. Complete CMC approval evidence unavailable.
caseStudies.rationale: Resubmission directly narrowed the population implicated by exposure concerns, with added CMC test data and prior drug approval. Residual manufacturing/PK risk prevents stronger than approval lean.

caseStudies.application: Supplemental BLA 761105/S-053, subcutaneous induction for Crohn's disease
caseStudies.phase: AFFIRM randomized placebo-controlled double-blind Phase 3 study, 289 patients.
caseStudies.evidence: Week 12 clinical remission approximately 55% versus 30%, and endoscopic response 44% versus 14%; both co-primary endpoints strongly significant.
caseStudies.benefitRisk: Self-administered SC route avoids infusion initiation; efficacy is demonstrated, with no new safety risks in sponsor's controlled trial disclosure.
caseStudies.regulatory: Existing FDA-approved molecule for Crohn's disease plus route-specific positive pivotal study. New device, pharmacokinetics, labeling, immunogenicity or inspections remain private evidence gaps.
caseStudies.rationale: Positive randomized route-specific efficacy and established safety support adding SC induction; no disclosed unresolved critical regulatory objections.
